title.zh: 卷30 列傳第22 竇熾 兄子毅 于翼 李穆
title.en: Volume 30 Biographies 22: Dou Chi; elder brother Ziyi; Yu Yi; Li Mu
title.raw: 卷30 列傳第22 竇熾 兄子毅 于翼 李穆 Volume 30 Biographies 22: Dou Chi; elder brother Ziyi; Yu Yi; Li Mu

sentences.zh: 竇熾 兄子毅 于翼 李穆

translations.literal: Dou Chi; elder brother's son Yi; Yu Yi; Li Mu
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chi; his nephew Yi; Yu Yi; Li Mu

sentences.zh: 竇熾字光成，扶風平陵人也。

translations.literal: Dou Chi, styled Guangcheng, was a native of Pingling in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chi, courtesy name Guangcheng, came from Pingling in Fufeng commandery.

sentences.zh: 漢大鴻臚章十一世孫。

translations.literal: Eleventh-generation descendant of Zhang, Grand Herald of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He was an eleventh-generation descendant of Zhang, who had served Han as grand herald.

sentences.zh: 章子統，靈帝時，為雁門太守，避竇武之難，亡奔匈奴，遂為部落大人。

translations.literal: Zhang's son Zitong, in Emperor Ling's time, was Administrator of Yanmen; fleeing the disaster of Dou Wu, he fled to the Xiongnu and became a tribal chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's son Zitong, under Emperor Ling, was administrator of Yanmen; fleeing the purge of Dou Wu, he took refuge among the Xiongnu and rose to lead a tribal confederation.

sentences.zh: 後魏南徙，子孫因家於代，賜姓紇豆陵氏。

translations.literal: When Later Wei moved south, his descendants made their home in Dai and were granted the surname Heldouling.
translations.idiomatic: When the Northern Wei moved south, the family settled in Dai and was granted the surname Heldouling.

sentences.zh: 累世仕魏，皆至大官。

translations.literal: For generations they served Wei, all reaching high office.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they served Wei, and every man among them reached high office.

sentences.zh: 父略，平遠將軍。

translations.literal: His father Lue was General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lue held the title General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 以熾著勳，贈少保、柱國大將軍、建昌公。

translations.literal: Because of Chi's distinguished merit, [Lue was] posthumously awarded Junior Guardian, Pillar-of-State Grand General, and Duke of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Dou Chi's achievements, Lue was posthumously made junior guardian, pillar-of-state grand general, and Duke of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 熾性嚴明，有謀略，美鬚髯，身長八尺二寸。

translations.literal: Chi's nature was stern and clear; he had stratagems; fine beard and whiskers; body height eight chi two cun.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Chi was stern and clear-minded, skilled in strategy, with a fine beard and a frame eight chi two cun tall.

sentences.zh: 少從范陽祁忻受《毛詩》、《左氏春秋》，略通大義。

translations.literal: In youth he studied the Mao Odes and Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals under Qi Xin of Fanyang, and broadly grasped their essential meaning.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied the Mao Odes and Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals under Qi Xin of Fanyang and gained a working grasp of their larger meaning.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，膂力過人。

translations.literal: Skilled at mounted archery; bodily strength surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at mounted archery and possessed strength beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 魏正光末，北鎮擾亂，熾乃隨畧避地定州，因沒於葛榮。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenguang of Wei, northern garrisons were in turmoil; Chi followed Lue in fleeing to Ding Province and was captured by Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenguang era, when the northern garrisons fell into chaos, Chi followed his father Lue to Ding Province and was taken by Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮欲官畧，畧不受。

translations.literal: Rong wished to grant Lue office; Lue would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong offered Lue an official post, but Lue refused it.

sentences.zh: 榮疑其有異志，遂留略於冀州，將熾及熾兄善隨軍。

translations.literal: Rong suspected he harbored a different intent, so detained Lue in Ji Province and took Chi and Chi's elder brother Shan with the army.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting disloyalty, Ge Rong kept Lue in Ji Province and took Chi and his elder brother Shan along with the army.

sentences.zh: 魏永安元年，爾朱榮破葛榮，熾乃將家隨榮於幷州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongan of Wei, Erzhu Rong defeated Ge Rong; Chi then brought his family to follow Rong at Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongan, after Erzhu Rong crushed Ge Rong, Chi moved his household to Bing Province in Erzhu Rong's train.

sentences.zh: 時葛榮別帥韓婁、郝長衆數萬人據薊城不下，以熾為都督，從驃騎將軍侯深討之。

translations.literal: At that time Ge Rong's subordinate commanders Han Lou and Hao Chang, with several tens of thousands, held Ji city and would not submit; Chi was made area commander and followed Flying Cavalry General Hou Shen to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong's lieutenants Han Lou and Hao Chang still held Ji with tens of thousands of men; Chi was made area commander and marched under Flying Cavalry General Hou Shen to besiege them.

sentences.zh: 熾手斬婁，以功拜揚烈將軍。

translations.literal: Chi personally beheaded Lou and for merit was appointed General Who Raises Glory.
translations.idiomatic: Chi cut down Han Lou with his own hand and, for that feat, was made General Who Raises Glory.

sentences.zh: 三年，除員外散騎侍郎，遷給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year, removed as Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders; transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered riders, then transferred to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 建明元年，加武厲將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianming, added title General Who Displays Martial Severity.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianming he received the additional title General Who Displays Martial Severity.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武卽位，茹茹等諸番竝遣使朝貢，帝臨軒宴之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei took the throne, Ruru and various barbarian peoples all sent envoys with tribute; the emperor feasted them at the imperial audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei succeeded, the Ruru and other frontier peoples all sent tribute missions, and the emperor held a feast for them in the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 有鴟飛鳴於殿前，帝素知熾善射，因欲示遠人，乃給熾御箭兩隻，命射之。

translations.literal: An owl flew screeching before the hall; the emperor had long known Chi was skilled at archery and wished to display this to distant peoples; he gave Chi two imperial arrows and ordered him to shoot it.
translations.idiomatic: An owl flew screeching before the hall. The emperor, who knew Chi's skill with the bow, wished to impress the foreign envoys and gave him two imperial arrows with orders to bring it down.

sentences.zh: 鴟乃應弦而落，諸番人咸歎異焉。

translations.literal: The owl fell at the release of the string; all the barbarian peoples sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: The bird dropped at the twang of the string, and the envoys from every quarter cried out in astonishment.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜帛五十疋。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor rewarded him with fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 尋率兵隨東南道行台樊子鵠追爾朱仲遠，仲遠奔梁。

translations.literal: Soon he led troops following the Southeast Circuit Inspector Fan Zigu in pursuit of Erzhu Zhongyuan; Zhongyuan fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he led troops under Southeast Circuit Inspector Fan Zigu in pursuit of Erzhu Zhongyuan, who fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 時梁主又遣元樹入寇，攻陷譙城，遂據之。

translations.literal: At that time the Liang ruler also sent Yuan Shu to invade; they attacked and took Qiao city and held it.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler then sent Yuan Shu to raid the borders; Qiao city was taken and held.

sentences.zh: 子鵠令熾率騎兵擊破之，封行唐縣子，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Zigu ordered Chi to lead cavalry and defeat them; he was enfeoffed Viscount of Xingtang County with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zigu ordered Chi to lead cavalry against them and break their force; Chi was enfeoffed Viscount of Xingtang with five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋拜直閤將軍、銀青光祿大夫，領華騮令，進爵上洛縣伯，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Soon appointed Direct Gate General, Silver Seal Grandee with Blue Ribbon, concurrently Warden of Hualiu; advanced to Baron of Shangluo County with fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made direct gate general and silver-seal grandee with blue ribbon, warden of Hualiu, and raised to Baron of Shangluo with one thousand feudal households.

sentences.zh: 時帝與齊神武構隙，以熾有威重，堪處爪牙之任，拜閤內大都督。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor and Gao Huan had a breach; because Chi had authority and weight, fit for claw-and-fang duties, he was appointed Grand Interior Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor and Gao Huan fell out, Chi's authority and presence made him fit for the hardest duties at court, and he was made grand interior commander.

sentences.zh: 遷撫軍將軍，朱衣直閤，遂從帝西遷。

translations.literal: Transferred to General Who Pacifies the Army, Red-Robe Direct Gate [General], and followed the emperor in the westward migration.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to general who pacifies the army and red-robe direct gate general, then followed the emperor in the flight west.

sentences.zh: 仍與其兄善重至城下，與武衛將軍高金龍戰於千秋門，敗之。

translations.literal: Still together with his elder brother Shan he returned to the city walls and fought Martial Guard General Gao Jinlong at Qianqiu Gate, defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Shan then rode back to the capital and, at Qianqiu Gate, defeated Martial Guard General Gao Jinlong.

sentences.zh: 因入宮城，取御馬四十疋幷鞍勒，進之行所。

translations.literal: Thereupon entered the palace city, took forty imperial horses together with saddles and bridles, and presented them at the emperor's traveling encampment.
translations.idiomatic: They entered the palace precinct, seized forty imperial horses with their tack, and delivered them to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，賜熾及善駿馬各二疋、駑馬十疋。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and bestowed on Chi and Shan each two fine horses and ten inferior horses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was overjoyed and gave Chi and Shan each two thoroughbreds and ten remounts.

sentences.zh: 高仲密以北豫州來附，熾率兵從太祖援之。

translations.literal: Gao Zhongmi came over with Northern Yu Province; Chi led troops following the Grand Progenitor to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi defected with Northern Yu Province, Chi led troops under Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai to support him.

sentences.zh: 至洛陽，會東魏人據邙山為陣，太祖命留輜重于瀍曲，率輕騎奮擊，中軍與右軍大破之，悉虜其步卒。

translations.literal: Reaching Luoyang, they encountered Eastern Wei men holding Mount Mang in battle array; the Grand Progenitor ordered baggage left at Chan Qu, led light cavalry in fierce attack; center and right armies greatly defeated them, capturing all their foot soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang they found Eastern Wei forces drawn up on Mount Mang. Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai left the baggage at Chan Qu and led light cavalry in a fierce charge; the center and right wings broke the enemy and took every foot soldier captive.

sentences.zh: 熾獨追至石濟而還。

translations.literal: Chi alone pursued as far as Shiji and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chi alone pursued as far as Shiji before turning back.

sentences.zh: 遷車騎大將軍、儀同三司、散騎常侍，增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Transferred to General of Chariots and Cavalry, honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders; fief increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of chariots and cavalry, regular attendant of the scattered riders, and honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, with one thousand more households added to his fief.

sentences.zh: 十三年，進使持節、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中，增邑通前三千九百戶。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, advanced to bearer of credentials, Grand General of Flying Cavalry, opening-office honors equal to Three Ducal Ministers, added Palace Attendant; fief increased in all to three thousand nine hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was raised to bearer of credentials, grand general of flying cavalry, and opening-office honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, with palace attendant added and his fief brought to three thousand nine hundred households in all.

sentences.zh: 出為涇州刺史，莅職數年，政號清淨。

translations.literal: Sent out as Inspector of Jing Province; holding office several years, administration was called pure and tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Posted out as inspector of Jing, he governed for several years in a manner praised as pure and quiet.

sentences.zh: 改封

translations.literal: Changed in enfeoffment to
translations.idiomatic: His fief was changed to

translations.literal: (Wu) [emended: Wu]
translations.idiomatic: [emended: Wu]

sentences.zh: 安〔武〕縣公，進授大將軍。

translations.literal: An (Wu) [emended: Wu] county duke, advanced to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Anwu county, with promotion to grand general.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝元年，除大都督、原州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Fei of Wei, removed as Grand Area Commander, Inspector of Yuan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Fei of Wei he was made grand area commander and inspector of Yuan Province.

sentences.zh: 熾抑挫豪右，申理幽滯，每親巡壟畝，勸民耕桑。

translations.literal: Chi suppressed and checked powerful families, clarified grievances of the wrongly detained, personally toured fields, and urged people in farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: Chi curbed the great clans, cleared cases long buried in obscurity, walked the fields himself, and urged the people toward plowing and mulberry work.

sentences.zh: 在州十載，甚有政績。

translations.literal: Ten years in the province, very much had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years in the province he had a record of real achievement.

sentences.zh: 州城之北，有泉水焉，熾屢經遊踐，嘗與僚吏宴於泉側，因酌水自飲曰：「吾在此州，唯當飲水而已。

translations.literal: North of the provincial city there was a spring; Chi often passed by it on his travels; once feasting with staff officials beside the spring, he poured water and drank, saying: "In this province I should only drink water, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: North of the provincial seat lay a spring Chi often visited on his rounds. Once, feasting there with his staff, he poured himself a cup of the water and said, "In this province I need ask for nothing but this water.

sentences.zh: 」及去職之後，人吏感其遺惠，每至此泉者，莫不懷之。

translations.literal: " After leaving office, officials and people moved by his lasting favor, all who came to this spring none did not cherish his memory.
translations.idiomatic: " After he left office, officials and commoners alike, moved by his legacy, never came to that spring without thinking of him.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝元年，進爵廣武郡公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei, advanced in rank to Duke of Guangwu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was raised to Duke of Guangwu commandery.

sentences.zh: 屬茹茹寇廣武，熾率兵與柱國趙貴分路討之。

translations.literal: When Ruru raided Guangwu, Chi led troops with Pillar-of-State Zhao Gui on separate routes to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ruru raided Guangwu, Chi marched with Pillar-of-State Zhao Gui on separate routes to drive them off.

sentences.zh: 茹茹聞軍至，引退。

translations.literal: Ruru heard the army had arrived and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Ruru withdrew as soon as they heard the army was coming.

sentences.zh: 熾度河至麴伏川追及，與戰，大破之，斬其酋帥郁久閭是發，獲生口數千，及雜畜數萬頭。

translations.literal: Chi crossed the river to Qufu River, caught up, fought, greatly defeated them, beheaded their chieftain Yujiuli Shifa, captured several thousand living captives and tens of thousands of miscellaneous livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Chi crossed the river, caught the enemy at Qufu River, and routed them; he beheaded their chieftain Yujiuli Shifa, took several thousand captives, and seized tens of thousands of livestock.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，增邑二千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, fief increased by two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, his fief was increased by two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 武成二年，拜柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wucheng, appointed Pillar-of-State Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In Wucheng year 2 he was made pillar-of-state grand general.

sentences.zh: 世宗以熾前朝忠勳，望實兼重，欲獨為造第。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong, because Chi had loyal merit from the previous dynasty, repute and substance both weighty, wished solely to build him a residence.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong, honoring Chi's loyal service under the previous reign and his weight in name and deed, wished to build him a mansion of his own.

sentences.zh: 熾辭以天下未定，干戈未偃，不宜輒發徒役，世宗不許。

translations.literal: Chi declined on grounds the realm was not settled, weapons of war not laid aside, not fitting to rashly dispatch corvee labor; Shizong did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Chi refused, saying the realm was still unsettled and arms not yet laid down, and that it was wrong to press corvee labor on the people; Shizong would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 尋而帝崩，事方得寢。

translations.literal: Soon the emperor died and the matter was only then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died soon afterward, the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 熾旣朝之元老，名位素隆，至於軍國大謀，常與參議。

translations.literal: Chi being an elder of the court, name and rank always eminent, as to major plans of army and state, he was constantly consulted.
translations.idiomatic: As an elder of the court whose name and rank had long stood high, he was regularly drawn into the great decisions of war and state.

sentences.zh: 嘗有疾，高祖至其第而問之，因賜金石之藥。

translations.literal: Once when ill, Emperor Gaozu came to his residence to inquire of him and bestowed mineral and herb medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when he fell ill, Emperor Gaozu came in person to his house to ask after him and gave him precious mineral and herbal medicines.

sentences.zh: 其見禮如此。

translations.literal: Such was the courtesy shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the honor he received.

sentences.zh: 帝於大德殿將謀伐齊，熾時年已衰老，乃扼腕曰：「臣雖朽邁，請執干櫓，首啟戎行。

translations.literal: The emperor at Dade Hall was about to plan attacking Qi; Chi's years were already aged; he gripped his wrist and said: "Your servant though decayed and advanced in years, asks to grasp shield and spear, first to open the military march.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor met at Dade Hall to plan the conquest of Qi, Chi, though old, clenched his wrist and said, "Your servant may be worn and white-haired, yet I beg to take up shield and spear and lead the army out.

sentences.zh: 得一睹誅翦鯨鯢，廓清寰宇，省方觀俗，登岳告成，然後歸魂泉壤，無復餘恨。

translations.literal: To gain one sight of executing and cutting down whales and minnows, clearing and purifying all within the heavens, making the tour of the regions and observing customs, ascending the peak and announcing completion, then returning my soul to the springs and earth — no further regret.
translations.idiomatic: Let me live to see the great beasts cut down and the realm swept clean, to tour the provinces and read the customs of the land, to climb the sacred peak and proclaim the deed accomplished — then I may return my soul to the earth with nothing left to regret.

sentences.zh: 」高祖壯其志節，遂以熾第二子武當公恭為左二軍總管。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu applauded his resolve and integrity, and thereupon made Chi's second son Gong, Duke of Wudang, commander of the Left Second Army.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Gaozu was stirred by his spirit and made Chi's second son Gong, Duke of Wudang, commander of the Left Second Army.

sentences.zh: 齊平之後，帝乃召熾歷觀相州宮殿。

translations.literal: After Qi was pacified, the emperor then summoned Chi to tour successively the palaces of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi fell, the emperor had Chi walk with him through the palaces of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 熾拜賀曰：「陛下真不負先帝矣。

translations.literal: Chi bowed in congratulation and said: "Your Majesty truly has not failed the former emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Chi bowed in congratulation and said, "Your Majesty has truly kept faith with the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅，賜奴婢三十人，及雜繒帛千疋，進位上柱國。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly pleased, bestowed thirty slaves and maidservants and one thousand bolts of miscellaneous silk, advanced in rank to Upper Pillar-of-State.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was delighted, gave him thirty slaves and maidservants and a thousand bolts of silk, and raised him to upper pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，兼雍州牧。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng, concurrently Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanzheng year 1 he was made concurrent governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝營建東京，以熾為京洛營作大監。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was building the Eastern Capital, Chi was made Grand Supervisor of Capital-Luo Construction.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan undertook the Eastern Capital project, Chi was made grand supervisor of the Luoyang works.

sentences.zh: 宮苑制度，皆取決焉。

translations.literal: Palace gardens and regulations all took his decision.
translations.idiomatic: The layout of palaces and gardens was settled on his judgment alone.

sentences.zh: 大象初，改食樂陵縣，邑戶如舊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daxiang, changed to draw sustenance from Leling County, fief households as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Daxiang era his income was shifted to Leling county while his feudal households remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝輔政，停洛陽宮作，熾請入朝。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui assisted the government, Luoyang palace construction was halted; Chi requested to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took power as regent and halted work on the Luoyang palaces, Chi asked leave to come to court.

sentences.zh: 屬尉遲迥舉兵，熾乃移入金墉城，簡練關中軍士得數百人，與洛州刺史、平涼西元亨同心固守，仍權行洛州鎮事。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong raised troops, Chi then moved into Jinyong city, selected and trained several hundred Guanzhong soldiers, together with Luozhou Inspector Xiwen Yuanheng of Pingliang held fast in one resolve, and concurrently acted as overseer of Luozhou garrison affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rose in arms, Chi withdrew into Jinyong, mustered several hundred Guanzhong troops, and with Luozhou inspector Xiwen Yuanheng of Pingliang held the city in common resolve while acting as provisional overseer of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 相州平，熾方入朝。

translations.literal: When Xiang Province was pacified, Chi then entered court.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Xiang Province was pacified did Chi enter court.

sentences.zh: 屬隋文帝初為相國，百官皆勸進。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui had just become Chief Minister, all officials urged him to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui had just become chief minister, the whole bureaucracy urged him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 熾自以累代受恩，遂不肯署牋。

translations.literal: Chi considering himself indebted for generations of grace, therefore would not sign the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Chi, mindful of generations of imperial favor, refused to sign the memorial of accession.

sentences.zh: 時人高其節。

translations.literal: People of the time esteemed his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the day praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 熾事親孝，奉諸兄以悌順聞。

translations.literal: Chi served parents with filiality, attended elder brothers with brotherly deference — renowned for this.
translations.idiomatic: He was filial toward his parents and deferential toward his elder brothers, and was famed for both.

sentences.zh: 及其位望隆重，而子孫皆處列位，遂為當時盛族。

translations.literal: When his position and repute were weighty, and sons and grandsons all held ranks, he thus became a great clan of the age.
translations.idiomatic: As his standing rose and sons and grandsons filled the ranks of office, the Dou became one of the great clans of the day.

sentences.zh: 子茂嗣。

translations.literal: His son Mao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 茂有弟十三人，恭、威最知名。

translations.literal: Mao had thirteen younger brothers; Gong and Wei were most famed.
translations.idiomatic: Mao had thirteen younger brothers; Gong and Wei were the best known.

sentences.zh: 恭位至大將軍。

translations.literal: Gong reached the rank of Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Gong rose to grand general.

sentences.zh: 從高祖平齊，封贊國公，除西兗州總管，以罪賜死。

translations.literal: Following Emperor Gaozu in pacifying Qi, enfeoffed Duke of Zan State, removed as Overall Commander of Western Yan Province, by crime granted death.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Gaozu in the conquest of Qi, was enfeoffed Duke of Zan, made overall commander of Western Yan, and was condemned to death for a crime.

sentences.zh: 熾兄善，以中軍大都督、南城公從魏孝武西遷。

translations.literal: Chi's elder brother Shan, as Grand Interior Commander of the Center Army and Duke of Nancheng, followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei in the westward migration.
translations.idiomatic: Chi's elder brother Shan, grand interior commander of the center army and Duke of Nancheng, followed Emperor Xiaowu of Wei in the flight west.

sentences.zh: 後仕至太僕、衛尉卿、汾北華瀛三州刺史、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、永富縣公。

translations.literal: Later served reaching Grand Master of Horsebreeding, Commandant of the Guard, inspector of three provinces Fenbei, Hua, and Ying, Grand General of Flying Cavalry, opening-office honors equal to Three Ducal Ministers, Duke of Yongfu County.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose through grand master of horsebreeding and commandant of the guard to inspector of Fenbei, Hua, and Ying, grand general of flying cavalry, opening-office honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, and Duke of Yongfu county.

sentences.zh: 諡曰忠。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子榮定嗣。

translations.literal: His son Rongding succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rongding succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 起家魏文帝千牛備身。

translations.literal: First entered service as Thousand-Ox Attendant of Emperor Wen of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as thousand-ox attendant to Emperor Wen of Wei.

sentences.zh: 稍遷平東將軍、大都督，進驃騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Gradually transferred to General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Area Commander; advanced to Grand General of Flying Cavalry, honors equal to Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He rose gradually to general who pacifies the east and grand area commander, then to grand general of flying cavalry with honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 歷佽飛中大夫、右司衛上大夫。

translations.literal: Served as Lieutenant of the Rapid Tiger Guard, Upper Grandee of the Right Office of Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He served as lieutenant of the rapid tiger guard and upper grandee of the right office of guards.

sentences.zh: 大象中，位至大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Daxiang era, reached the rank of Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daxiang era he reached grand general.

sentences.zh: 熾兄子毅。

translations.literal: Chi's elder brother's son Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Chi's nephew Yi.

sentences.zh: 毅字天武。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Tianwu.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, courtesy name Tianwu.

sentences.zh: 父岳，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Yue died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yue died young.

sentences.zh: 及毅著勳，追贈大將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yi achieved merit, [Yue was] posthumously awarded Grand General and Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi earned distinction, Yue was posthumously made grand general and inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 毅深沉有器度，事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: Yi was deep and steady with capacity and breadth; served parents — famed for filiality.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was deep, steady, and broad-minded, and was known above all for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武初，起家為員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, first entered service as Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei's reign he entered service as supernumerary regular attendant of the scattered riders.

sentences.zh: 時齊神武擅朝，毅慨然有殉主之志。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Huan monopolized the court; Yi sighed deeply and had the will to die for his lord.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan then dominated the court, and Yi burned with the resolve to die for his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，遂從入關，封奉高縣子，邑六百戶，除符璽郎。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu migrated west, he then followed into the passes, enfeoffed Viscount of Fenggao County with fief of six hundred households, removed as Keeper of Seals and Credentials.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu fled west, Yi followed him into the passes, was enfeoffed Viscount of Fenggao with six hundred households, and was made keeper of seals and credentials.

sentences.zh: 從擒竇泰，復弘農，戰沙苑，皆有功。

translations.literal: Following in the capture of Dou Tai, recovering Hongnong, fighting at Shaye — all had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at the capture of Dou Tai, the recovery of Hongnong, and the battle of Shaye, earning merit in each.

sentences.zh: 拜右將軍、太中大夫，進爵為侯，增邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Appointed General of the Right, Grand Master of Palace Counsel; advanced in rank to marquis; fief increased by one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of the right and grand master of palace counsel, raised to marquis, and given one thousand more households.

sentences.zh: 累遷持節、撫軍將軍、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Repeatedly transferred to bearer of credentials, General Who Pacifies the Army, Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and the Scattered Riders.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through bearer of credentials, general who pacifies the army, and regular attendant of direct communication and the scattered riders.

sentences.zh: 魏廢帝二年，授車騎大將軍、儀同三司、大都督，進爵安武縣公，增邑一千四百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei, granted General of Chariots and Cavalry, honors equal to Three Ducal Ministers, Grand Area Commander; advanced to Duke of Anwu County; fief increased by fourteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Fei of Wei he was granted general of chariots and cavalry, honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, and grand area commander, raised to Duke of Anwu county, with fourteen hundred households added to his fief.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝元年，進授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、大都督，改封永安縣公，出為幽州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he was advanced to Grand General of the Flying Cavalry, opened a grand mastership equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, made grand area commander, changed enfeoffment to Duke of Yong'an County, and sent out as Inspector of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was promoted to Grand General of the Flying Cavalry, given a grand mastership equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, made grand area commander, re-enfeoffed Duke of Yong'an, and sent out as inspector of You.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，進爵神武郡公，增邑通前五千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was advanced in rank to Duke of Shenwu commandery, and his fief was increased to five thousand households in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin came to the throne, he was raised to Duke of Shenwu, with a combined fief of five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，徵還朝，治左宮伯，轉小宗伯，尋拜大將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding, he was recalled to court, administered the Left Palace Guard, transferred to Junior Clan Commander, and soon appointed Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoding he was recalled to court, put in charge of the Left Palace Guard, moved to junior clan commander, and soon made grand general.

sentences.zh: 時與齊人爭衡，戎車歲動，竝交結突厥，以為外援。

translations.literal: At that time, in rivalry with the men of Qi, war chariots moved every year; both sides alike allied with the Turks as an external aid.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou and Northern Qi were locked in rivalry, campaigning year after year, and both courted the Turks as allies.

sentences.zh: 在太祖之時，突厥已許納女于我，齊人亦甘言重幣，遣使求婚。

translations.literal: In Grand Progenitor's time the Turks had already promised to give a daughter to us; the men of Qi also used sweet words and heavy gifts and sent envoys to seek marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Under Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai the Turks had already promised a bride; Qi too sent envoys with fine words and rich gifts to ask for a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 狄固貪婪，便欲有悔。

translations.literal: The Di were by nature greedy and at once wished to repent of it.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks, greedy by nature, soon wanted to go back on their word.

sentences.zh: 朝廷乃令楊薦等累使結之，往反十餘，方復前好。

translations.literal: The court then ordered Yang Jian and others to go repeatedly on missions to bind them; more than ten round trips passed before the former friendship was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Yang Jian and others on mission after mission; only after more than ten round trips was the old friendship restored.

sentences.zh: 至是，雖期往逆，猶懼改圖。

translations.literal: Even then, though the date for going to receive her was set, they still feared a change of plan.
translations.idiomatic: Even when the day came to go and escort the bride back, the court still feared the Turks might change their minds.

sentences.zh: 以毅地兼勛戚，素有威重，乃命為使。

translations.literal: Because Yi's territory and merit were combined with imperial kinship, and he had long possessed authority and weight, he was appointed envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yi combined territorial power with imperial connections and had long commanded respect, he was chosen as envoy.

sentences.zh: 及毅之至，齊使亦在焉。

translations.literal: When Yi arrived, the Qi envoy was also there.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi reached the Turk court, Qi's envoy was there as well.

sentences.zh: 突厥君臣，猶有貳志。

translations.literal: The Turk ruler and his ministers still harbored divided loyalties.
translations.idiomatic: The Turk ruler and his ministers were still of two minds.

sentences.zh: 毅抗言正色，以大義責之，累旬乃定，卒以皇后歸。

translations.literal: Yi spoke forthrightly with stern countenance, rebuking them on grounds of righteousness; only after many days was the matter settled, and in the end the empress was sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Yi spoke out boldly, his face stern, and upbraided them in the name of righteousness; after many days the matter was settled and the bride was sent to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 朝議嘉之，別封成都縣公，邑一千戶，進位柱國。

translations.literal: The court praised this; he was separately enfeoffed Duke of Chengdu County with a fief of one thousand households and advanced to pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended him, gave him a separate fief as Duke of Chengdu with one thousand households, and promoted him to pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 出為同州刺史，遷蒲州總管，徙金州總管，加授上柱國，入為大司馬。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Inspector of Tong Province, transferred to area commander of Pu, moved to area commander of Jin, additionally given senior pillar-of-state, and recalled as Grand Marshal of the State.
translations.idiomatic: He served as inspector of Tong, then as area commander of Pu and Jin, was given senior pillar-of-state, and returned to court as grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，拜定州總管。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang under Sui, he was appointed area commander of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Kaihuang era under Sui he was made area commander of Ding.

sentences.zh: 累居藩鎮，咸得民和。

translations.literal: Over many terms in frontier commands, he always won the people's accord.
translations.idiomatic: Through long service on the frontiers he always kept the people on his side.

sentences.zh: 二年，薨於州，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the second year he died in his province at age sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he died in office at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 贈襄郢等六州刺史，諡曰肅。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the six prefectures of Xiang, E, and others; his posthumous title was Su.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as governor of Xiang, E, and four other prefectures, with the posthumous name Su.

sentences.zh: 毅性溫和，每以謹慎自守，又尚太祖第五女襄陽公主，特為朝廷所委信。

translations.literal: Yi's nature was mild; he always guarded himself with caution, and because he had married Grand Progenitor's fifth daughter, Princess Xiangyang, he was especially entrusted by the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was even-tempered and habitually cautious; as the husband of Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's fifth daughter, Princess Xiangyang, he enjoyed the court's special trust.

sentences.zh: 雖任兼出入，未嘗有矜惰之容，時人以此稱焉。

translations.literal: Though his duties took him in and out of office, he never showed a proud or lazy bearing; men of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: However often he moved between court and command, he never showed arrogance or slackness, and his contemporaries admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 子賢嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 賢字托賢，志業通敏，少知名。

translations.literal: Xian, styled Tuoxian, had aims and accomplishments that were penetrating and quick, and from youth he was known.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, styled Tuoxian, was quick and capable, and was known from an early age.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，策拜神武國世子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, by examination he was appointed heir of the Shenwu state.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhe he passed the examination and was made heir of the Shenwu state.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，授使持節儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng, he was given the title bearer of the staff of authority, General equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanzheng he was made bearer of the staff of authority and general equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，襲爵神武公，除遷州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang period under Sui, he inherited the title Duke of Shenwu and was appointed Inspector of Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui in the Kaihuang era he succeeded as Duke of Shenwu and was appointed inspector of Qian.

sentences.zh: 于翼字文若，太師、燕公謹之子。

translations.literal: Yu Yi, styled Wenruo, was a son of the Grand Preceptor and Duke of Yan, Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi, styled Wenruo, was the son of Grand Preceptor Yu Jin, Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 美風儀，有識度。

translations.literal: He had fine bearing and discernment.
translations.idiomatic: He had handsome presence and sound judgment.

sentences.zh: 年十一，尚太祖女平原公主，拜員外散騎常侍，封安平縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: At age eleven he married Grand Progenitor's daughter, Princess Pingyuan, was appointed Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Outside the Office, and enfeoffed Duke of Anping County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he married Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's daughter, Princess Pingyuan, was made regular attendant of scattered cavalry outside the office, and enfeoffed Duke of Anping with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 大統十六年，進爵郡公，加大都督，領太祖帳下左右，禁中宿衛。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Datong, he was advanced in rank to commandery duke, made grand area commander, and put in charge of the left and right of Grand Progenitor's personal guard, on overnight duty within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Datong he was promoted to commandery duke and grand area commander, and placed over the left and right of Grand Progenitor's personal guard on palace watch.

sentences.zh: 遷鎮南將軍、金紫光祿大夫、散騎常侍、武衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Guards the South, Grandee of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Guards the South, gold-seal grandee, regular attendant of scattered cavalry, and general of the martial guard.

sentences.zh: 謹平江陵，所贈得軍實，分給諸子。

translations.literal: When Jin pacified Jiangling, the military stores received as gifts were divided among his sons.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Jin took Jiangling, the captured stores were divided among his sons.

sentences.zh: 翼一無所取，唯簡賞口內名望子弟有士風者，別待遇之。

translations.literal: Yi took none of it; he only selected captives among those of name and family with the air of gentlemen and treated them separately with honor.
translations.idiomatic: Yi took nothing for himself; he singled out only captives of good family with a scholar's bearing and treated them with special regard.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，特賜奴婢二百口，翼固辭不受。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor heard of this, he specially granted two hundred households of slaves and servants; Yi firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, hearing of this, offered him two hundred households of slaves and servants; Yi firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 尋授車騎大將軍、儀同三司，加侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, and additionally made Palace Attendant, Grand General of the Flying Cavalry, and opened a grand mastership equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made General of Chariots and Cavalry with honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, then additionally palace attendant, Grand General of the Flying Cavalry, and a grand mastership equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 六官建，除左宮伯。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was appointed Left Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Six Offices were set up he was made Left Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，出為渭州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he was sent out as Inspector of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin came to the throne, he was sent out as inspector of Wei.

sentences.zh: 翼兄寔先蒞此州，頗有惠政。

translations.literal: Yi's elder brother Shi had previously come to this province and had a reputation for benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's elder brother Shi had governed the province before him and was known for benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 翼又推誠布信，事存寬簡，夷夏感悅，比之大小馮君焉。

translations.literal: Yi again extended sincerity and spread trust; in affairs he kept to leniency and simplicity; barbarians and Chinese alike were moved and pleased, comparing him to the two Lords Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Yi in turn ruled with sincerity and trust, keeping administration light and humane; Chinese and non-Chinese alike were delighted and compared him to the two Lords Feng.

sentences.zh: 時吐谷渾入寇河右，涼鄯河三州咸被攻圍，使來告急。

translations.literal: At that time Tuyuhun invaded the right bank of the Yellow River; the three prefectures of Liang, Shan, and He were all besieged, and messengers came reporting urgency.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun raided the Hexi region, Liang, Shan, and He were all besieged and urgent appeals arrived.

sentences.zh: 秦州都督遣翼赴援，不從。

translations.literal: The area commander of Qin sent Yi to go to the rescue; he did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin area commander ordered Yi to march to the rescue; he refused.

sentences.zh: 寮屬咸以為言。

translations.literal: All his staff spoke against this.
translations.idiomatic: Every member of his staff objected.

sentences.zh: 翼曰：「攻取之術，非夷俗所長。

translations.literal: Yi said: "The art of storming and taking places is not what barbarian custom excels at.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Barbarians are not skilled at siege warfare.

sentences.zh: 此寇之來，不過抄掠邊牧耳。

translations.literal: This band, in coming, can do no more than raid and plunder the frontier pastures.
translations.idiomatic: These raiders have come only to loot the border pastures.

sentences.zh: 安能頓兵城下，久事攻圍！

translations.literal: How could they halt their army below the walls and long pursue siege?
translations.idiomatic: They cannot sit under our walls in a long siege.

sentences.zh: 掠而無獲，勢將自走。

translations.literal: If they raid and gain nothing, the momentum will make them withdraw of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: If they find nothing to take, they will withdraw on their own.

sentences.zh: 勞師以往，亦無所及。

translations.literal: To weary the army by going there would also achieve nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Marching out to meet them would only exhaust our troops for no gain.

sentences.zh: 翼揣之已了，幸勿復言。

translations.literal: I have already calculated this through; pray do not speak of it again."
translations.idiomatic: I have already thought this through; say no more about it."

sentences.zh: 」居數日問至，果如翼所策。

translations.literal: After several days inquiry arrived, and it was indeed as Yi had forecast.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the reports came in, exactly as Yi had predicted.

sentences.zh: 賀蘭祥討吐谷渾，翼率州兵先鋒深入。

translations.literal: When Helan Xiang attacked Tuyuhun, Yi led the prefectural troops as vanguard and penetrated deep.
translations.idiomatic: When Helan Xiang campaigned against Tuyuhun, Yi led the prefectural army as vanguard deep into enemy country.

sentences.zh: 以功增邑一千二百戶。

translations.literal: For merit his fief was increased by one thousand two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service his fief grew by one thousand two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋徵拜右宮伯。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned and appointed Right Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and made Right Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 世宗雅愛文

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong deeply loved letters and
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong had a deep love of letters and

translations.literal: 〔literature〕 [emended: history]
translations.idiomatic: [Textual note: wen 文 emended to shi 史]

sentences.zh: 〔史〕，立麟趾學，在朝有藝業者，不限貴賤，皆預聽焉。

translations.literal: 〔History〕; he established the Linchi Academy, and all in court who had artistic accomplishment, without limit of noble or base, were admitted to hear lectures.
translations.idiomatic: history; he founded the Linchi Academy, and every man at court with real learning, regardless of rank, was invited to attend.

sentences.zh: 乃至蕭撝、王褒等與卑鄙之徒同為學士。

translations.literal: Thus even Xiao Kui, Wang Bao, and others were fellows with low and vulgar men as academy scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Even men like Xiao Kui and Wang Bao sat as fellow scholars beside common opportunists.

sentences.zh: 翼言於帝曰：「蕭撝，梁之宗子；

translations.literal: Yi spoke to the emperor, saying: "Xiao Kui is a scion of Liang;
translations.idiomatic: Yi told the emperor, "Xiao Kui is a prince of Liang;

sentences.zh: 王褒，梁之公卿。

translations.literal: Wang Bao is a minister of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao is a Liang court minister.

sentences.zh: 今與趨走同儕，恐非尚賢貴爵之義。

translations.literal: Now to be peers with runners and attendants — I fear this is not the meaning of honoring the worthy and valuing rank.
translations.idiomatic: To rank them alongside men who scurry at others' heels hardly honors worth and rank as it should.

sentences.zh: 」帝納之，詔翼定其班次，於是有等差矣。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted this and ordered Yi to fix their seating order; thereafter there were distinctions of rank.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed and ordered Yi to set their order of precedence; from then on the academy had proper gradations.

sentences.zh: 晉公護以帝委翼腹心，內懷猜忌。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Hu, because the emperor entrusted Yi as a trusted confidant, harbored suspicion within.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, seeing the emperor rely on Yi as a trusted confidant, grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 轉為小司徒，加拜柱國。

translations.literal: Yi was transferred to Junior Minister of Education and additionally appointed pillar-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was moved to junior minister of education and additionally made pillar-of-state.

sentences.zh: 雖外示崇重，實疎斥之。

translations.literal: Though outwardly shown lofty honor, in reality he was pushed aside.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he was honored; in fact he was sidelined.

sentences.zh: 及誅護，帝召翼，遣往河東取護子中山公訓，仍代鎮蒲州。

translations.literal: When Hu was executed, the emperor summoned Yi, sent him to Hedong to fetch Hu's son Duke of Zhongshan Xun, and had him replace the garrison at Pu.
translations.idiomatic: After Hu was killed, the emperor summoned Yi, sent him to Hedong to bring back Hu's son, Duke of Zhongshan Xun, and had him take command at Pu in Hu's place.

sentences.zh: 翼曰：「冢宰無君陵上，自取誅夷。

translations.literal: Yi said: "The chief minister was without a ruler and lords it above his sovereign; he brought execution on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "The regent defied his sovereign and brought ruin on himself.

sentences.zh: 元惡旣除，餘孽宜殄。

translations.literal: Once the chief evil is removed, the remaining offspring ought to be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the chief culprit is gone, his remaining kin ought to be wiped out.

sentences.zh: 然皆陛下骨肉，猶謂疎不間親。

translations.literal: Yet they are all Your Majesty's own flesh and blood; one still says that distant kin cannot come between close kin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they are Your Majesty's own kin, and the rule holds that kin should not be set against kin.

sentences.zh: 陛下不使諸王而使臣異姓，非直物有橫議，愚臣亦所未安。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not send one of the princes but sends me, a man of another surname, it is not only that the world will murmur — this foolish minister also is not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty sends me, a man of another surname, rather than one of the princes, the court will talk — and I myself would be uneasy.

sentences.zh: 」帝然之，乃遣越王盛代翼。

translations.literal: " The emperor agreed and then sent Prince of Yue Sheng to replace Yi.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed and sent Prince of Yue Sheng in Yi's place.

sentences.zh: 先是，與齊陳二境，各修邊防，雖通聘好，而每歲交兵。

translations.literal: Earlier, on the borders with Qi and Chen, each side repaired frontier defenses; though envoys passed in friendship, every year there was fighting.
translations.idiomatic: On the Qi and Chen frontiers both sides had long fortified their borders; envoys still came and went, but armies clashed every year.

sentences.zh: 然一彼一此，不能有所克獲。

translations.literal: Yet first on one side, then on the other, neither could achieve capture or gain.
translations.idiomatic: Yet victory shifted back and forth, and neither side could win a lasting gain.

sentences.zh: 高祖旣親萬機，將圖東討，詔邊城鎮，竝益儲偫，加戍卒。

translations.literal: After Gaozu personally took charge of affairs and planned an eastern campaign, he ordered the frontier fortresses and garrisons all to increase stored supplies and add garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Gaozu took personal control and planned an eastern offensive, he ordered every frontier fortress to stockpile supplies and reinforce its garrisons.

sentences.zh: 二國聞之，亦增修守禦。

translations.literal: When the two states heard this, they also increased repairs of defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and Chen heard of it and strengthened their defenses in turn.

sentences.zh: 翼諫曰：「宇文護專制之日，興兵至洛，不戰而敗，所喪實多。

translations.literal: Yi remonstrated, saying: "In the days when Yuwen Hu held sole power, he raised troops as far as Luoyang, and without fighting was defeated; what was lost was truly great.
translations.idiomatic: Yi urged caution: "When Yuwen Hu ruled alone he marched as far as Luoyang and was beaten without a battle — the loss was enormous.

sentences.zh: 數十年委積，一朝麋散。

translations.literal: Stores accumulated over decades were scattered in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Decades of accumulated stores vanished in a morning.

sentences.zh: 雖為護無制勝之策，亦由敵人之有備故也。

translations.literal: Though it was because Hu had no strategy for certain victory, it was also because the enemy was prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Hu lacked a winning strategy, but the enemy was also ready.

sentences.zh: 且疆埸相侵，互有勝敗，徒損兵儲，非策之上者。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the borders encroach on one another and victory and defeat alternate, it only wastes troops and stores — this is not the highest policy.
translations.idiomatic: Border skirmishes that trade victories back and forth only waste men and grain — that is no wise policy.

sentences.zh: 不若解邊嚴，減戎防，繼好息民，敬待來者。

translations.literal: Better to relax frontier alerts, reduce frontier garrisons, renew friendship and give the people rest, and respectfully await what comes.
translations.idiomatic: Better to stand down the frontier, cut garrisons, restore friendly relations, let the people recover, and wait courteously for the other side.

sentences.zh: 彼必

translations.literal: They will surely
translations.idiomatic: They are certain to

translations.literal: 〔good/shan〕 [emended: pleased/xi]
translations.idiomatic: [Textual note: shan 善 emended to xi 喜]

sentences.zh: 〔喜〕於通和，懈而少備，然後出其不意，一舉而山東可圖。

translations.literal: 〔Pleased〕 at renewed harmony, relax their guard and make light preparations; then strike where they do not expect it, and in one move the east of the mountains can be taken.
translations.idiomatic: be pleased at renewed peace, slacken their guard, and then be taken by surprise — in one stroke the lands east of the mountains can be won.

sentences.zh: 若猶習前蹤，恐非蕩定之計。

translations.literal: If we still follow the old track, I fear this is not the plan for sweeping pacification.
translations.idiomatic: If we repeat the old approach, I fear we will never secure the east.

sentences.zh: 」帝納之。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 建德二年，出為安隨等六州五防諸軍事、安州總管。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiande, he was sent out as commander-in-chief of the six prefectures of An, Sui, and others with five frontier defenses, and area commander of An.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiande he was sent out to command the six prefectures of An, Sui, and others with their five frontier defenses, as area commander of An.

sentences.zh: 時屬大旱，溳水絕流。

translations.literal: At that time there was great drought; the Yun River ceased to flow.
translations.idiomatic: A great drought struck, and the Yun River ran dry.

sentences.zh: 舊俗，每逢亢陽，禱白兆山祈雨。

translations.literal: By old custom, whenever there was blazing sun, they prayed for rain at Mount Baizhao.
translations.idiomatic: By local custom, whenever drought lingered, the people prayed for rain at Mount Baizhao.

sentences.zh: 高祖先禁群祀，山廟已除。

translations.literal: Gaozu had first forbidden mass sacrifices; the mountain shrine had already been removed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu had banned popular sacrifices, and the mountain shrine had been dismantled.

sentences.zh: 翼遣主簿祭之，卽日澍雨霑洽，歲遂有年。

translations.literal: Yi sent his chief clerk to sacrifice there; that very day timely rain fell in abundance, and the year had a harvest.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent his chief clerk to offer sacrifice there; rain fell the same day, and the year brought a good harvest.

sentences.zh: 民庶感之，聚會歌舞，頌翼之德。

translations.literal: The people were moved by this; they gathered, sang, and danced, praising Yi's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people were so grateful that they gathered to sing and dance, praising Yi's virtue.

sentences.zh: 四年，高祖將東伐，朝臣未有知者，遣納言盧韞等前後乘驛，三詣翼問策焉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Gaozu was about to campaign east; the court ministers did not yet know it; he sent Direct Speech Officer Lu Yun and others, riding post relays before and after, three times to Yi to ask his strategy.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, as Emperor Gaozu prepared an eastern campaign in secret, he sent Direct Speech Officer Lu Yun and others by post relay three times to ask Yi's counsel — though no other minister yet knew of the plan.

sentences.zh: 翼贊成之。

translations.literal: Yi supported and approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Yi endorsed the plan.

sentences.zh: 及軍出，詔翼率荊、楚兵二萬，自宛、葉趣襄城，大將軍張光洛、鄭恪等竝隸焉。

translations.literal: When the army set out, an edict ordered Yi to lead twenty thousand troops of Jing and Chu from Wan and Ye toward Xiangcheng; Grand Generals Zhang Guangluo, Zheng Ke, and others were all placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched, an edict ordered Yi to lead twenty thousand Jing and Chu troops from Wan and Ye toward Xiangcheng, with Grand Generals Zhang Guangluo, Zheng Ke, and others under his command.

sentences.zh: 旬日下齊一十九城。

translations.literal: In ten days he took nineteen Qi cities.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he captured nineteen Qi cities.

sentences.zh: 所部都督，輒入民村，卽斬以狥。

translations.literal: Whenever a commander under him entered a civilian village, he was immediately beheaded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Any subordinate commander who entered a civilian village was beheaded on the spot as an example.

sentences.zh: 由是百姓欣悅，赴者如歸。

translations.literal: Because of this the common people were pleased and delighted; those who came to join were like returning home.
translations.idiomatic: The people welcomed him gladly, and volunteers flocked to him as though coming home.

sentences.zh: 屬高祖有疾，班師，翼亦旋鎮。

translations.literal: Because Gaozu fell ill, the army withdrew; Yi also returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu fell ill the army turned back, and Yi returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 五年，轉陝熊等七州十六防諸軍事、宜陽總管。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was transferred to commander-in-chief of the seven prefectures of Shan and Xiong with sixteen frontier defenses, and area commander of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was transferred to command the seven prefectures of Shan and Xiong with sixteen frontier defenses, as area commander of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 翼以宜陽地非襟帶，請移鎮於陝。

translations.literal: Yi, because Yiyang's terrain was not a strategic choke point, requested to move the command to Shan.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Yiyang poorly situated as a strategic base, Yi asked to move headquarters to Shan.

sentences.zh: 詔從之，仍除陝州刺史，總管如舊。

translations.literal: An edict followed this; he was additionally appointed Inspector of Shan, and his area command remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed; Yi was also made inspector of Shan while keeping his area command.

sentences.zh: 其年，大軍復東討，翼自陝入九曲，攻拔造澗等諸城，徑到洛陽。

translations.literal: That year the great army again campaigned east; Yi from Shan entered Jiuchu, attacked and took Zaojian and other cities, and went straight to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when the main army marched east again, Yi advanced from Shan through Jiuchu, took Zaojian and other cities, and pushed straight to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 齊洛州刺史獨孤永業開門出降，河南九州三十鎮，一時俱下。

translations.literal: Qi's Inspector of Luo, Dugu Yongye, opened the gates and came out to surrender; the nine prefectures and thirty garrisons of Henan all fell at once.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's Luo inspector, Dugu Yongye, opened the gates and surrendered; the nine prefectures and thirty garrisons of Henan fell in one stroke.

sentences.zh: 襄城民庶等喜復見翼，竝壺漿塞道。

translations.literal: The common people of Xiangcheng and elsewhere rejoiced to see Yi again; together they brought jars of drink and filled the road.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xiangcheng and the surrounding districts rejoiced to see Yu Yi again, bringing jars of drink to line the road.

sentences.zh: 尋卽除洛懷等九州諸軍事、河陽總管。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed commander-in-chief of military affairs for the nine prefectures Luo, Huai, and others, and area commander of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commander-in-chief of military affairs for Luo, Huai, and seven other prefectures, and area commander of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 尋徙豫州總管，給兵五千人、馬千疋以之鎮，並配開府及儀同等二十人。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to area commander of Yu, given five thousand troops and one thousand horses to garrison with, and assigned twenty officers with grand masterships and ranks equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to area commander of Yu, given five thousand troops and one thousand horses for his garrison, and assigned twenty opening-office and equal-to-three-ducal-minister officers.

sentences.zh: 仍勑河陽、襄州、安州、荊州

translations.literal: An edict still ordered the area commanders within Heyang, Xiang, An, and Jing provinces
translations.idiomatic: An edict further ordered the area commanders of Heyang, Xiang, An, and Jing provinces

translations.literal: (Si) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Si]

sentences.zh: 州總管內有武幹者，任翼徵牒，不限多少。

translations.literal: that any within them who had military talent were to be summoned by Yi on requisition, without limit on numbers.
translations.idiomatic: and Si, that any man of military talent might be requisitioned by Yu Yi without limit on numbers.

sentences.zh: 儀同以下官爵，承制先授後聞。

translations.literal: For offices and titles below equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, he was empowered by commission to grant them first and report afterward.
translations.idiomatic: For ranks below equal-to-three-ducal-minister status, he was authorized to appoint first and report afterward.

sentences.zh: 陳將魯天念久圍光州，聞翼到汝南，望風退散。

translations.literal: The Chen general Lu Tiannian had long besieged Guang Province; hearing that Yi had reached Runan, he dispersed at the mere report.
translations.idiomatic: Chen general Lu Tiannian had long besieged Guang Province; when he learned Yu Yi had reached Runan, his force melted away.

sentences.zh: 霍州蠻首田元顯，負險不賓，於是，送質請附。

translations.literal: Tian Yuanxian, chieftain of the barbarians of Huo Province, relying on rugged terrain and refusing submission, thereupon sent hostages and asked to attach himself.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yuanxian, a Huo barbarian chieftain who had held difficult ground and refused submission, then sent hostages and asked to submit.

sentences.zh: 陳將任蠻奴悉衆攻顯，顯立柵拒戰，莫有異心。

translations.literal: The Chen general Ren Mannu attacked Xian with his full force; Xian built a stockade and resisted, and none wavered in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Chen general Ren Mannu attacked him with his full force; Tian Yuanxian fortified a camp and fought back without a defection.

sentences.zh: 及翼還朝，元顯便叛。

translations.literal: When Yi returned to court, Yuanxian at once rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yu Yi returned to court, Tian Yuanxian rebelled at once.

sentences.zh: 其得殊俗物情，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His grasp of the sentiments of foreign lands was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His understanding of frontier peoples was always like this.

sentences.zh: 大象初，徵拜大司徒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daxiang, he was summoned and appointed Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Daxiang era he was summoned and made grand minister of education.

sentences.zh: 詔翼巡長城，立亭鄣。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yi to patrol the Great Wall and establish watch towers and border posts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Yu Yi to inspect the Great Wall and establish watchtowers and border posts.

sentences.zh: 西自鴈門，東至碣石，創新改舊，咸得其要害云。

translations.literal: From Wild Goose Gate in the west to Jieshi in the east, creating new ones and altering old ones, all obtained their key points, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: From Wild Goose Gate in the west to Jieshi in the east he rebuilt old posts and established new ones at every strategic point.

sentences.zh: 仍除幽定七州六鎮諸軍事、幽州總管。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed commander-in-chief of military affairs for the seven prefectures You and Ding with six garrisons, and area commander of You.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made commander-in-chief of military affairs for You, Ding, and five other prefectures with six garrisons, and area commander of You.

sentences.zh: 先是，突厥屢為寇掠，居民失業。

translations.literal: Earlier the Turks had repeatedly raided and plundered, and the people had lost their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks had repeatedly raided the region, and the people had lost their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 翼素有威武，兼明斥候，自是不敢犯塞，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Yi had long possessed martial authority and was also skilled in reconnaissance; from then on they did not dare violate the frontier, and the common people were secure.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi had long commanded respect as a soldier and was skilled in scouting; thereafter the Turks dared not cross the border, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 及尉遲迥據相州舉兵，以書招翼。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong held Xiang Province and raised troops, he sent a letter to recruit Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong seized Xiang Province and rebelled, he sent Yu Yi a letter inviting him to join.

sentences.zh: 翼執其使，幷書送之。

translations.literal: Yi detained the envoy and sent the letter along with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi detained the envoy and forwarded the letter to the court.

sentences.zh: 于時隋文帝執政，賜翼雜繒一千五百段、粟麥一千五百石，幷珍寶服玩等，進位上柱國，封任國公，增邑通前五千戶，別食任城縣一千戶，收其租賦。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wen of Sui directed the government; he granted Yi one thousand five hundred bolts of mixed silk and one thousand five hundred shi of grain and wheat, together with treasures, garments, and curios; advanced him to senior pillar-of-state; enfeoffed him Duke of Ren State; increased his fief together with the former to five thousand households; separately fed Rencheng county one thousand households and collected its rents and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui, then directing the government, rewarded Yu Yi with fifteen hundred bolts of mixed silk, fifteen hundred shi of grain and wheat, and treasures and fine goods; raised him to senior pillar-of-state; enfeoffed him Duke of Ren; brought his combined fief to five thousand households; granted him a separate maintenance fief of one thousand households in Rencheng county; and allowed him its rents.

sentences.zh: 翼又遣子讓通表勸進，幷請入朝。

translations.literal: Yi also sent his son Rang with a memorial urging accession, and requested to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi also sent his son Rang with a memorial urging Yang Jian to take the throne and asked leave to come to court.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝許之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui agreed.

sentences.zh: 翼性恭儉，與物無競，常以滿盈自戒，故能以功名終。

translations.literal: Yi's nature was respectful and frugal; he did not compete with others, and constantly warned himself against fullness; therefore he was able to finish with merit and reputation intact.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi was modest and frugal, never striving against others, and always guarded himself against excess; thus he kept his rank and reputation to the end.

sentences.zh: 子璽，官至上大將軍、軍司馬、黎陽郡公。

translations.literal: His son Xi reached supreme grand general, army commandant, and Duke of Liyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi rose to supreme grand general, army commandant, and Duke of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 璽弟詮，上儀同三司、吏部下大夫、常山公。

translations.literal: Xi's younger brother Quan was upper equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, lower grandee of the Ministry of Personnel, and Duke of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's younger brother Quan held upper equal-to-three-ducal-minister rank, served as lower grandee of the Ministry of Personnel, and was Duke of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 詮弟讓，儀同三司。

translations.literal: Quan's younger brother Rang held rank equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Rang, his younger brother, stood equal to the Three Dukes in rank.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥之舉兵也，河西公李賢弟穆為幷州總管，亦執迥子送之。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong raised troops, Duke of Hexi Li Xian's younger brother Mu, as area commander of Bing, also detained Jiong's son and sent him in.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, Li Mu, younger brother of Duke of Hexi Li Xian and area commander of Bing, likewise seized Jiong's son and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 李穆字顯慶，少明敏，有度量。

translations.literal: Li Mu, styled Xianqing, from youth was bright and keen and had measure.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu, styled Xianqing, was clever and steady-minded from youth.

sentences.zh: 太祖入關，便給事左右，深被親遇。

translations.literal: When Grand Progenitor entered the Pass, Mu was at once assigned to attend left and right and was deeply favored.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai entered the Pass, Li Mu was immediately placed in his personal service and enjoyed deep favor.

sentences.zh: 穆亦小心謹肅，未嘗懈怠。

translations.literal: Mu also was careful, respectful, and solemn, and never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu was careful, respectful, and never slack in duty.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，遂處以腹心之任，出入臥內，當時莫與為比。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor praised this and thereupon placed him in a trusted inner duty; he entered and left the bedchamber, and at the time none could compare with him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai approved and put him in the innermost circle of trust, admitting him to the sleeping quarters; at the time no one stood higher in favor.

sentences.zh: 及侯莫陳悅害賀拔岳，太祖自夏州赴難，而悅黨史歸據原州，猶為悅守。

translations.literal: When Hou Mo Chen Yue killed Heba Yue, Grand Progenitor came from Xia Province to the rescue; Yue's partisan Shi Gui held Yuan Province and still defended it for Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Mo Chen Yue killed Heba Yue, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai marched from Xia Province to the rescue; Yue's follower Shi Gui held Yuan Province and still defended it for Yue.

sentences.zh: 太祖令侯莫陳崇輕騎襲之。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor ordered Hou Mo Chen Chong to raid him with light cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ordered Hou Mo Chen Chong to strike with light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 穆先在城中，與兄賢、遠等據城門應崇，遂擒歸。

translations.literal: Mu was already in the city; with his elder brother Xian, Yuan, and others he held the gate to meet Chong, and thus captured Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu was already inside the city; with his elder brother Xian, Yuan, and the others he held the gate open for Chong and captured Shi Gui.

sentences.zh: 以功授都督。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed area commander.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was made area commander.

sentences.zh: 從迎魏孝武，封永平縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: Following in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu of Wei, he was enfeoffed Baron of Yongping county with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When he helped welcome Emperor Xiaowu of Wei westward, he was enfeoffed Baron of Yongping with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 擒竇泰，復弘農，並有戰功。

translations.literal: Capturing Dou Tai and recovering Hongnong both counted as battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: He shared in the capture of Dou Tai and the recovery of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之捷，穆又言于太祖曰：「高歡今日已喪膽矣，請速逐之，則歡可擒也。

translations.literal: At the victory at Shaya, Mu again spoke to Grand Progenitor, saying: "Gao Huan today has already lost his nerve; please pursue quickly, and Huan can be captured.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory at Shaya, Li Mu again told Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, "Gao Huan has lost his nerve today; pursue at once and he can be taken.

sentences.zh: 」太祖不聽。

translations.literal: " Grand Progenitor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 論前後功，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Weighing earlier and later merit, he was advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: When his earlier and later services were weighed together, he was raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 河橋之戰，太祖所乘馬中流矢驚逸，太祖墜于地，軍中大擾。

translations.literal: In the battle at He Bridge, the horse Grand Progenitor rode was struck by a flying arrow, startled, and bolted; Grand Progenitor fell to the ground, and great disorder arose in the army.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of He Bridge, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's mount took an arrow, panicked, and bolted; he was thrown to the ground and the army fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 敵人追及之，左右皆奔散，穆乃以策抶太祖，因大罵曰：「爾曹主何在？

translations.literal: The enemy caught up; those left and right all scattered and fled; Mu then whipped Grand Progenitor with his riding crop and loudly cursed, saying: "Where is your master?
translations.idiomatic: The enemy closed in; his attendants scattered; Li Mu then struck Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai with his whip and shouted, "Where is your master?

sentences.zh: 爾獨住此！

translations.literal: You alone stay here!
translations.idiomatic: Why do you stand here alone!

sentences.zh: 」敵人不疑是貴人也，遂捨之而過。

translations.literal: " The enemy did not suspect he was a man of rank and therefore let him pass.
translations.idiomatic: " The pursuers did not guess he was a great man and rode on past.

sentences.zh: 穆以馬授太祖，遂得俱免。

translations.literal: Mu gave his horse to Grand Progenitor, and thus both escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu gave Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai his own horse, and both escaped.

sentences.zh: 是日微穆，太祖已不濟矣。

translations.literal: But for Mu that day, Grand Progenitor would already have been beyond saving.
translations.idiomatic: But for Li Mu that day, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai would not have survived.

sentences.zh: 自是恩盼更隆。

translations.literal: From then on favor and regard were even greater.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his favor was even greater.

sentences.zh: 擢授武衛將軍，加大都督、車騎大將軍、儀同三司，進爵

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed General of the Martial Guard, given the added posts of grand area commander, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and rank equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, and advanced in noble rank
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of the martial guard, given grand area commander, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and rank equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, and raised in noble rank

translations.literal: (Wu) [emended variant]
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Wu]

sentences.zh: 安〔武〕郡公，增邑一千七百戶。

translations.literal: [An] Wu commandery duke, fief increased by one thousand seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: to Duke of Anwu, with a fief increased by one thousand seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 前後賞賜，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Rewards before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The rewards that followed were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 久之，太祖美其志節，乃歎曰：「人之所貴，唯身命耳，李穆遂能輕身命之重，濟孤於難。

translations.literal: After a long time Grand Progenitor admired his loyalty and integrity and sighed, saying: "What people value is only body and life; Li Mu was able to treat the weight of body and life lightly and save the isolated one in difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai praised his loyalty and sighed, "All men value nothing above life itself; yet Li Mu could treat his life as light and save his lord in peril.

sentences.zh: 雖復加之以爵位，賞之以玉帛，未足為報也。

translations.literal: Even if one adds rank to him and rewards him with jade and silk, it is not enough to repay him.
translations.idiomatic: Rank and jade and silk could never repay what he did.

sentences.zh: 」乃特賜鐵券，恕以十死。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was specially granted an iron tally, pardoning up to ten capital offenses.
translations.idiomatic: " He was thereupon given a special iron tally pardoning up to ten capital offenses.

sentences.zh: 進驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、侍中。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand General of the Flying Cavalry, opened a grand mastership equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, and made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand General of the Flying Cavalry, given a grand mastership equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, and made palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，穆授太祖以驄馬，其後中廄有此色馬者，悉以賜之。

translations.literal: At first, when Mu gave Grand Progenitor a piebald horse, afterward whenever the imperial stud had horses of that color, all were granted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mu had first given Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai a piebald horse, every horse of that color in the imperial stud was afterward granted to him.

sentences.zh: 又賜穆世子惇安樂郡公，姊一人為郡君，余姊妹竝為縣君，兄弟子侄及緦麻以上親幷舅氏，皆沾厚賜。

translations.literal: He also granted Mu's heir Dun the title Duke of Anle commandery; one elder sister was made a commandery lady; the remaining sisters were all made county ladies; brothers' sons and nephews and relatives within five degrees of mourning, together with maternal uncles, all received generous gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He also made Li Mu's heir Dun Duke of Anle; one elder sister became a commandery lady and the rest county ladies; brothers, nephews, relatives within five degrees of mourning, and maternal kin all received rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 其見褒崇如此。

translations.literal: The honor and exaltation he received were to this extent.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the honor shown him.

sentences.zh: 從解玉壁圍，拜安定國中尉。

translations.literal: Following in the relief of the siege of Yubi, he was appointed Middle Commandant of Anding State.
translations.idiomatic: After the relief of Yubi he was made middle commandant of Anding State.

sentences.zh: 尋授同州刺史，入為太僕卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Inspector of Tong Province and entered court as Grand Master of Travelling Horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made inspector of Tong and recalled as grand master of travelling horses.

sentences.zh: 征江陵功，封一子長城縣侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: For merit in the Jiangling campaign, one son was enfeoffed Marquis of Changcheng county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For his service in the Jiangling campaign one son was enfeoffed Marquis of Changcheng with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋進位大將軍，賜姓拓拔氏。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to grand general and granted the surname Tuoba.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to grand general and granted the surname Tuoba.

sentences.zh: 俄除原州刺史，又以賢子為平高郡守，遠子為平高縣令，竝加鼓吹。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed as Inspector of Yuan Province; Xian's son was also made administrator of Pinggao commandery, and Yuan's son was made magistrate of Pinggao county; both were given added musical escort.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon relieved as inspector of Yuan; Li Xian's son was made administrator of Pinggao commandery and Li Yuan's son magistrate of Pinggao county, each with the added honor of a musical escort.

sentences.zh: 穆自以叔侄一家三人，皆牧宰鄉里，恩遇過隆，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: Mu himself, because uncle and nephews, three men of one family, all governed their native district, and favor exceeded what was proper, firmly declined and would not accept appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu himself, seeing uncle and two nephews of one family all governing their home region and favor running beyond custom, firmly declined the appointments.

sentences.zh: 太祖不許。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 後轉雍州刺史，入為小冢宰。
