translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Inspector of Yong Province and entered court as lesser grand steward.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to inspector of Yong and recalled as lesser grand steward.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，增邑通前三千七百戶，又別封一子為縣伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, his fief was increased together with the former to three thousand seven hundred households, and one son was separately enfeoffed county earl.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin came to the throne, Li Mu's combined fief reached three thousand seven hundred households and one son was separately enfeoffed as a county earl.

sentences.zh: 穆請迴封賢子孝軌，許之。

translations.literal: Mu requested that the enfeoffment be returned to Xian's son Xiaogui; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu asked that the new fief go to Li Xian's son Xiaogui, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 及遠子植謀害晉公護，植誅死，穆亦坐除名。

translations.literal: When Yuan's son Zhi plotted to harm Duke of Jin Hu, Zhi was executed, and Mu was also implicated and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yuan's son Zhi plotted against Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu, Zhi was executed and Li Mu was implicated and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 時植弟基任淅州刺史，例合從坐。

translations.literal: At the time Zhi's younger brother Ji was Inspector of Xi Province; by rule he should have shared the punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's younger brother Ji was then inspector of Xi and, by law, should have shared the punishment.

sentences.zh: 穆頻詣護，請以子惇、怡等代基死，辭理酸切，聞者莫不動容。

translations.literal: Mu repeatedly went to Hu and asked to substitute his sons Dun, Yi, and others for Ji's death; his words and reasoning were bitterly moving, and those who heard were all stirred.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu went repeatedly to Yuwen Hu and asked that his sons Dun and Yi die in Ji's place; his plea was so anguished that all who heard were moved.

sentences.zh: 護矜之，遂特免基死。

translations.literal: Hu took pity on him and specially exempted Ji from death.
translations.idiomatic: Hu took pity on him and specially spared Ji.

sentences.zh: 世宗卽位，拜驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、大都督、安武郡公、直州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, Mu was appointed Grand General of the Flying Cavalry, opened a grand mastership equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, made grand area commander, Duke of Anwu commandery, and Inspector of Zhi Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong came to the throne, Li Mu was made Grand General of the Flying Cavalry with a grand mastership equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, grand area commander, Duke of Anwu, and inspector of Zhi.

sentences.zh: 武成二年，拜少保。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wucheng, he was appointed Junior Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wucheng he was appointed junior preceptor.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, he was advanced to grand general.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding he was promoted to grand general.

sentences.zh: 三年，從隨公楊忠東伐。

translations.literal: In the third year, he followed Duke of Sui Yang Zhong in the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 he followed Duke of Sui Yang Zhong on the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 還，拜小司徒，遷柱國大將軍，別封一子郡公，邑二千戶。

translations.literal: On returning, he was appointed Junior Minister of Education, transferred to pillar-of-state grand general, and one son was separately enfeoffed commandery duke with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made junior minister of education, then pillar-of-state grand general, and one son was separately enfeoffed as a commandery duke with two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷大司空。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was transferred to Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was transferred to grand minister of works.

sentences.zh: 天和二年，進封申國公，邑五千戶，舊爵迴授一子。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianhe, he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Shen State with a fief of five thousand households; the old title was returned to one son.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianhe he was raised to Duke of Shen with five thousand households, and his old title passed to one son.

sentences.zh: 建德元年，遷太保。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiande, he was transferred to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiande he was made grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 尋出為原州總管。

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as area commander of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted out as area commander of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 四年，高祖東征，令穆率兵三萬，別攻軹關及河北諸縣，竝破之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Gaozu campaigned east and ordered Mu to lead thirty thousand troops in a separate attack on Zhiguan Pass and the counties of Hebei; all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, when Emperor Gaozu marched east, he ordered Li Mu to lead thirty thousand men in a separate attack on Zhiguan Pass and the Hebei counties; all fell.

sentences.zh: 後以帝疾班師，棄而不守。

translations.literal: Later, because the emperor fell ill, the army withdrew; the places taken were abandoned and not held.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill the army withdrew, and the captured posts were abandoned.

sentences.zh: 六年，進位上柱國，除幷州總管。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was advanced to senior pillar-of-state and appointed area commander of Bing.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was raised to senior pillar-of-state and made area commander of Bing.

sentences.zh: 時東夏再平，人情尚擾，穆鎮之以靜，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: At the time the eastern regions had just been pacified again, and popular sentiment was still unsettled; Mu governed them with calm, and the people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: The east had only just been pacified again and the people were still unsettled; Li Mu governed with calm, and they came to trust him.

sentences.zh: 大象元年，遷大左輔，總管如舊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daxiang, he was transferred to Grand Left Assistant, and his area command remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daxiang he was made grand left assistant while keeping his area command.

sentences.zh: 二年，加太傅，仍總管。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was given the added title Grand Tutor and still held area command.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 he was additionally made grand tutor and retained his area command.

sentences.zh: 及尉遲迥舉兵，穆子榮欲應之。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong raised troops, Mu's son Rong wished to respond to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, Li Mu's son Rong wanted to join him.

sentences.zh: 穆弗聽曰：「周德旣衰，愚智共悉。

translations.literal: Mu would not listen and said: "Zhou virtue has already declined; wise and foolish alike know it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu refused and said, "Zhou's virtue is spent; wise and foolish alike know it.

sentences.zh: 天時若此，吾豈能違天。

translations.literal: When heaven's season is like this, how can I go against heaven?
translations.idiomatic: When heaven's mandate runs this way, how can I defy heaven?

sentences.zh: 」乃遣使謁隋文帝，幷上十三環金帶，蓋天子之服也，以微申其意。

translations.literal: " He thereupon sent an envoy to pay court to Emperor Wen of Sui and presented a thirteen-ring gold belt — essentially the Son of Heaven's garment — to subtly express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent an envoy to Emperor Wen of Sui and offered a thirteen-ring gold belt — the sort worn by the Son of Heaven — as a subtle sign of submission.

sentences.zh: 時迥子誼為朔州刺史，亦執送京師。

translations.literal: At the time Jiong's son Yi was Inspector of Shuo Province; he too was detained and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jiong's son Yi was inspector of Shuo; he too was seized and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 迥令其所署行台韓長業攻陷潞州，執刺史趙威，署城民郭子勝為刺史。

translations.literal: Jiong ordered the field secretariat he had appointed, Han Changye, to attack and take Lu Province, detain Inspector Zhao Wei, and appoint the city resident Guo Zisheng as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong ordered his acting field secretariat chief Han Changye to take Lu Province, seize inspector Zhao Wei, and install the townsman Guo Zisheng as governor.

sentences.zh: 穆遣兵討之，獲子勝。

translations.literal: Mu sent troops to attack him and captured Zisheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu sent troops against him and captured Guo Zisheng.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝嘉之，以穆勞效同破鄴城第一勳，加三轉，聽分授其二子榮、才及兄賢子孝軌。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui praised this; because Mu's labor and achievement matched first merit in taking Ye city, he was given three added rank turns and permitted to distribute them to his two sons Rong and Cai and to Xian's son Xiaogui.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui commended him; treating Li Mu's service as equal to first merit in the fall of Ye, he granted three rank advances and allowed them to be divided among his sons Rong and Cai and Li Xian's son Xiaogui.

sentences.zh: 榮及才竝儀同大將軍，孝軌進開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: Rong and Cai were both grand generals equal to the Three Ducal Ministers; Xiaogui was advanced to grand general with a grand mastership equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Cai both became grand generals equal to the Three Ducal Ministers; Xiaogui was raised to grand general with a grand mastership equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 又別封子雄為密國公，邑三千戶。

translations.literal: One son, Xiong, was separately enfeoffed Duke of Mi State with a fief of three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Another son, Xiong, was separately enfeoffed Duke of Mi with three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 穆長子惇，字士宇。

translations.literal: Mu's eldest son Dun, styled Shiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu's eldest son Dun was styled Shiyu.

sentences.zh: 大統四年，以穆功賜爵安平縣侯，尋授車騎大將軍、儀同三司、大都督，進爵為公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Datong, for Mu's merit he was granted noble rank as Marquis of Anping county; soon he was appointed Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, and grand area commander, and advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Datong, for Li Mu's service Dun was enfeoffed Marquis of Anping; he was soon made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry with rank equal to the Three Ducal Ministers and grand area commander, and then raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 太祖令功臣世子並與略陽公遊處，惇于時輩之中，特被引接。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor ordered that the heirs of meritorious ministers all keep company with Duke of Lüeyang; among youths of that generation, Dun was specially favored and received.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai ordered the sons of meritorious ministers to keep company with Duke of Lüeyang Yuwen Jue; among his peers, Li Dun was singled out for special favor.

sentences.zh: 每有遐方服玩，異域珍奇，無不班錫。

translations.literal: Whenever there were garments and playthings from distant regions or exotic rare curiosities from foreign lands, none failed to be distributed and bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever exotic garments, playthings, and rarities arrived from distant lands, Dun was always among those rewarded.

sentences.zh: 俄

translations.literal: Soon afterward
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward,

translations.literal: (Receive) [emended: Appoint]
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Receive]

sentences.zh: 〔授〕小武伯，進爵安樂郡公。

translations.literal: 〔Appoint〕 Junior Wu Bo, advanced in rank to Duke of Anle commandery.
translations.idiomatic: he was made Junior Wu Bo and raised to Duke of Anle commandery.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、鳳州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe, he was transferred to Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Opening-office Equal-in-three-departments, and Inspector of Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe he was made grand general of agile cavalry, opening-office equal-in-three-departments, and inspector of Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卒於位。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died while holding his post.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍、原靈豳三州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand General and Governor of the three provinces Yuan, Ling, and Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously made grand general and governor of Yuan, Ling, and Bin provinces.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：竇熾儀錶魁梧，器識雄遠。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Dou Chi's bearing was imposing and dignified, his capacity and insight far-reaching and bold.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Dou Chi was imposing in bearing, bold and far-sighted in mind.

sentences.zh: 入參朝政，則嘉謀以陳；

translations.literal: When entering to take part in court government, excellent plans would be presented;
translations.idiomatic: At court he offered excellent counsel;

sentences.zh: 出總蕃條，則惠政斯洽。

translations.literal: when going out to oversee frontier administration, benevolent governance was thoroughly effective.
translations.idiomatic: in frontier office his benevolent rule won full compliance.

sentences.zh: 竇毅忠肅奉上，溫恭接下，茂實彰於本朝，義聲揚於殊俗。

translations.literal: Dou Yi served the throne with loyal devotion and treated subordinates with gentle courtesy; solid merit was displayed at the native court and righteousness resounded among foreign peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yi served the throne with loyal devotion and treated subordinates with gentle courtesy; solid merit shone at court and his righteous name rang among foreign peoples.

sentences.zh: 並以國華民望，論道當官，榮映一時，慶流來葉。

translations.literal: Both were national ornaments and popular hopes, holding office to expound the Way; glory shone for a generation and blessing flowed to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Both were ornaments of the state and men the people looked to; holding high office they expounded the Way, their glory lighting an age and their blessing flowing to later generations.

sentences.zh: 及熾遲疑勸進，有送故之心，雖王公恨恨，何以加此。

translations.literal: As for Chi's hesitation in urging enthronement and his mind of seeing off the former lord—even princes and dukes in resentful grief could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Chi hesitated to urge a new enthronement and kept a loyal heart toward the deposed sovereign, even princes and dukes consumed by resentment could hardly have gone further.

sentences.zh: 語曰：「君使臣以禮，臣事君以忠。

translations.literal: The saying goes: "The lord employs his ministers with ritual; ministers serve their lord with loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The saying goes, "The lord employs his ministers with ritual; ministers serve their lord with loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」然則效忠之跡或殊，處臣之理斯一，榷言指要，其維致命乎。

translations.literal: " Thus the traces of loyalty may differ, yet the principle of standing as minister is one—briefly speaking to the point, is it not a matter of giving one's life?
translations.idiomatic: " Loyalty may take different forms, but the duty of a minister is one—put simply, does it not come down to giving one's life?

sentences.zh: 是以典午擅朝，葛公休為之投袂；

translations.literal: Hence when Sima seized the court, Lord Zhuge Dan flung aside his sleeve in response;
translations.idiomatic: When the Sima clan monopolized Jin, Zhuge Dan took up arms;

sentences.zh: 新都篡盜，翟仲文所以稱兵。

translations.literal: when Wang Mang usurped and stole the throne, Zhai Zhongwen therefore raised armies.
translations.idiomatic: when Wang Mang seized the Han throne, Zhai Zhongwen took up arms in response.

sentences.zh: 及東郡誅夷，竟速漢朝之禍；

translations.literal: When Dong commandery was exterminated and purged, it hastened the calamity of the Han house;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Dan's destruction at Dong commandery hastened the Han dynasty's fall;

sentences.zh: 淮南覆敗，無救魏室之亡。

translations.literal: when Huainan collapsed in defeat, it could not save the Wei house from perishing.
translations.idiomatic: and his defeat at Huainan could not save the house of Wei.

sentences.zh: 而烈士貞臣，赴蹈不已，豈忠義所感，視死如歸者歟。

translations.literal: Yet martyrs and loyal ministers pressed forward without cease—was it not the pull of loyalty and righteousness, seeing death as going home?
translations.idiomatic: Yet loyal men pressed on without cease—surely righteousness alone can make a man welcome death as homecoming.

sentences.zh: 于、李之送往事居，有曲於此。

translations.literal: In Yu and Li's seeing off the old and serving the new, there is a twist in this.
translations.idiomatic: In Yu Yi and Li Mu's shift from serving the fallen order to the new one, the case is sadly different.

sentences.zh: 翼旣功臣之子，地卽姻親；

translations.literal: Yi was both son of a meritorious minister and by position a marriage kinsman;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi was both the son of a founding minister and, by marriage ties, kin to the throne;

sentences.zh: 穆乃早著勳庸，深寄肺腑。

translations.literal: Mu from early times had shown distinguished service and was deeply entrusted as a heart-and-guts confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu had won distinction early and was trusted as a close confidant.

sentences.zh: 並兼文武之任，荷累世之恩，理宜與存與亡，同休同戚。

translations.literal: Both held civil and military posts together, bore grace across generations—it was right they should live and die with the dynasty, sharing joy and sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Both held high civil and military posts, owed grace across generations, and should have shared the dynasty's fate in life and death.

sentences.zh: 加以受扞城之托，總戎馬之權，勢力足以勤王，智能足以衛難。

translations.literal: Added to this they received the charge of defending cities and held overall authority over armies and horses; their power was enough to rescue the throne, their capacity enough to ward off disaster.
translations.idiomatic: They held charges to defend the realm and command armies—power enough to rescue the throne, wit enough to meet danger.

sentences.zh: 乃宴安寵祿，曾無釋位之心；

translations.literal: Yet they rested content in favor and emolument, never once having the mind to yield their posts;
translations.idiomatic: Yet they clung to favor and salary and never thought of stepping aside;

sentences.zh: 報使獻誠，但務隨時之義。

translations.literal: They sent envoys offering loyalty, but only pursued the principle of following the times.
translations.idiomatic: they sent envoys pledging loyalty, but only followed the expedient of the moment.

sentences.zh: 弘名節以高貴，豈所望於二公。

translations.literal: To magnify fame and integrity into high nobility—is that what was expected of these two lords?
translations.idiomatic: Was this the loyalty expected of such exalted ministers?

sentences.zh: 若捨彼天時，徵諸人事，顯慶起晉陽之甲，文若發幽薊之兵，叶契岷峨，約從漳滏，北控沙漠，西指崤函，則成敗之數，未可量也。

translations.literal: If one set aside Heaven's timing and sought evidence in human affairs—Xianqing raising troops at Jinyang, Wenruo deploying forces from You and Ji, keeping pact with Min and E, joining alliance from Zhang and Fu, controlling the desert north and pointing at Xiaohan west—then whether success or defeat prevailed could not be measured.
translations.idiomatic: If one set timing aside and looked to human causes—had Xianqing raised the standard at Jinyang and Wenruo marched from You and Ji, joined allies from Min and E, drawn support from the Zhang and Fu region, held the northern desert and struck toward Xiaohan—no one could say how the contest would have ended.
